feed.title: Articles — Pablo Correa Prieto
feed.subtitle: Articles by Pablo Correa Prieto on artificial intelligence in teachers’ work.

entry.title: Detecting AI in a student’s work: why reliability is not the question
entry.summary: Detectors have improved, and that settles nothing: a probability about a text cannot ground a decision about a student.

entry.title: What makes a response work: the information, not the grade
entry.summary: More than 38% of feedback effects are negative. What makes the difference is how much information is carried, not the grade.

entry.title: Acceptance is not use: what surveys on AI in schools actually measure
entry.summary: Acceptance surveys measure an intention validated against a self-report. Self-reported use tracks logged use poorly.

entry.title: Marking with AI: compare it with our real errors, not with perfection
entry.summary: A century of research on human marking, and what it means for using AI as a second reader.

entry.title: A correct item is not necessarily aligned: three questions for judging an assessment item
entry.summary: Alignment, cognitive demand, quality: three separate questions for judging an item against the PER.

entry.title: Protect the effort that makes learning happen: what to hand to AI, what to keep demanding
entry.summary: Desirable difficulties and the first studies on AI in class: what effort does for learning.

entry.title: Preparing fast with AI: the real work is checking
entry.summary: AI saves preparation time; the real work is checking the objective, the level of demand and accuracy.

entry.title: What AI really changes for teachers who prepare and assess
entry.summary: Prepare, assess, learn: three shifts AI brings to teachers’ work.
